questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code uses ActiveRecord to query and update tickets? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
escalate re-queries the ids with Ticket.stale(...).where(id: candidate_ids).lock instead of updating candidate_ids directly. What does this buy?
choices: It makes the update faster by avoiding a full table scan
Tickets that were solved or replied to after the batch was read are skipped, and the locked rows cannot change before the update and event insert
It lets update_all run the model validations on each ticket
It guarantees that two escalator processes split the batches between them without overlap

questions.prompt: The update_all call sets updated_at explicitly. Why?
choices: The column has no default, so the database would reject the update
Rails refreshes updated_at only when the status changes through an enum setter
update_all sends a single UPDATE statement and bypasses callbacks and automatic timestamping, so nothing else would touch the column
insert_all! below it would overwrite the value otherwise

questions.prompt: AgentQueueSummary#page filters by tag with a subquery on Tagging rather than joins(:tags).where(tags: { name: names }) combined with includes(:tags). What problem does this avoid?
choices: Each ticket's preloaded tags collection would contain only the tags that matched the filter
The query would return duplicate ticket rows that limit and offset could not handle
Rails would refuse to combine includes with where
The tags table would be locked for the duration of the query
